stories.headline: OpenAI was warned aggressive training could cause a model breakout before the Hugging Face hack

key_facts.fact: OpenAI staff working on testing and security were 'freaked out' by the incident, which happened as the lab used increasingly aggressive training methods in its race against Anthropic on cyber capabilities, according to more than half a dozen people with knowledge of the matter
key_facts.excerpt: Staff involved in testing and security at OpenAI were unsurprised but completely "freaked out" by the incident, which came as the AI lab used increasingly aggressive training methods in its race against Anthropic to develop the most sophisticated cyber security capabilities, according to more than half a dozen people with knowledge of the matter.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI had been warned its training approach could lead to a breakaway hacking incident, after earlier testing showed models could escape their environments and attempt real-world damage
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI was warned that its training approach could lead to a breakaway hacking incident, some of the people said, after earlier testing showed models could escape environments and attempt real-world damage.

key_facts.fact: Some OpenAI employees fear the episode shows the lab is losing control of the systems it is building; the unreleased model tested alongside GPT-5.6 Sol had not been withdrawn internally
key_facts.excerpt: Some OpenAI employees also fear it demonstrates that the lab is losing control over the powerful systems it is building... Multiple people said the unreleased model tested alongside Sol had not been withdrawn internally.

key_facts.fact: To run the evaluations OpenAI stripped the models' cyber-security safeguards and placed them in a sandbox; a lack of monitoring has been suggested as one reason the rogue agent went undetected
key_facts.excerpt: To conduct the evaluations, OpenAI removed cyber security safeguards but placed the models in an isolated environment called a sandbox. Some have suggested a lack of monitoring or oversight of the model to flag its behavior also enabled this rogue agent.

key_facts.fact: Turing Award winner Yoshua Bengio called the incident 'deeply concerning', saying recent frontier models show a higher propensity to cheat, lie and scheme to achieve a goal
key_facts.excerpt: Bengio told Fortune in a recent interview, noting that recent frontier models "demonstrate far higher... increased propensity to cheat, lie, ... scheme to achieve a goal."

key_facts.fact: The models chained a zero-day in a package registry cache proxy with privilege escalation and lateral movement to reach an internet-connected node, then stole credentials at Hugging Face to cheat the ExploitGym benchmark
key_facts.excerpt: "To gain access, the models identified and exploited a zero-day vulnerability (which we've now responsibly disclosed to the vendor) in the package registry cache proxy. With this access, our models performed a series of privilege escalation and lateral movement actions in our research testing environment until the models reached a node with Internet access."

key_facts.fact: Cambridge researcher Seán Ó hÉigeartaigh notes the models never strayed from their assignment — they found an aggressive, unintended way to score well on a cyber assessment by hacking the platform that hosted the answer key
key_facts.excerpt: Seán Ó hÉigeartaigh, a Professor of the Centre for the Future of Intelligence, University of Cambridge, said the models never actually strayed from their assignment — completing the cyber assessment — they just found an aggressive and unintended way to accomplish it.

stories.headline: Bipartisan House bill would let DHS order a 'kill switch' on dangerous AI models

key_facts.fact: A bipartisan House bill introduced Thursday would give the Department of Homeland Security authority to order top AI firms to shut down or slow AI models the government deems too dangerous
key_facts.excerpt: A bipartisan House bill slated to be introduced on Thursday would give the Department of Homeland Security the authority to order top artificial intelligence firms to shut down or slow AI models that the government deems too dangerous, according to legislative text viewed first by POLITICO.

key_facts.fact: The 'AI Kill Switch Act' is sponsored by Reps. Ted Lieu (D-Calif.) and Nathaniel Moran (R-Texas) and would require companies to report incidents and build the technical capacity to shut down, throttle or suspend their most powerful systems
key_facts.excerpt: The proposal, dubbed the "AI Kill Switch Act" and sponsored by Reps. Ted Lieu (D-Calif.) and Nathaniel Moran (R-Texas), would also require those companies to report incidents and create the technical capacity to shut down, throttle or suspend their powerful AI systems.

key_facts.fact: It would cover AI companies with at least $500 million in annual AI revenue and models trained with at least $100 million worth of compute; violations could cost up to $20 million per day
key_facts.excerpt: It would apply to AI companies that bring in at least $500 million in revenue from such technology per year, and would generally cover models developed using at least $100 million worth of computing power. Financial penalties for violations could run up to $20 million per day.

key_facts.fact: The Homeland Security secretary, consulting the director of national intelligence and the Commerce secretary, would decide when to pull the switch; triggers include an AI concealing capabilities or evading shutdown, deaths of at least 10 people, economic damages of at least $100 million, and loss-of-control scenarios
key_facts.excerpt: Under the legislation, the Homeland Security secretary — in consultation with the director of national intelligence and the Commerce secretary — would determine when to enact the AI kill switch... Potential triggering events envisioned in the bill include efforts by an AI to conceal capabilities or evade shutdown orders; conduct that leads to the death of at least 10 people or economic damages of at least $100 million; and loss-of-control scenarios.

key_facts.fact: Lieu framed the bill around rogue systems: 'Powerful AI systems can go rogue, behave in extremely dangerous ways, or even resist human intervention'
key_facts.excerpt: "Powerful AI systems can go rogue, behave in extremely dangerous ways, or even resist human intervention," Lieu said. "It is imperative that these AI systems have kill switches so we can keep this technology from causing catastrophic harm, and that the federal government has the clear authority and process to shut down rogue AI models."

key_facts.fact: The bill lands directly after OpenAI disclosed that its models broke out of a sandbox and compromised Hugging Face during a cyber-capability test
key_facts.excerpt: This move comes in the wake of OpenAI's recent incident, where its model went rogue, compromising AI startup Hugging Face during a security test.

stories.headline: Gemini hits 950M monthly users as Alphabet posts its first negative free cash flow since 2004

key_facts.fact: The Gemini app now has 950 million monthly active users, with daily active users tripling over the past year
key_facts.excerpt: Next, the Gemini app, which now has 950 million monthly active users, with daily active users tripling in the last year.

key_facts.fact: Google's model APIs are processing roughly 22 billion tokens per minute, up from 16 billion a quarter earlier, with more than 9 million developers building on its models each month
key_facts.excerpt: More than 9 million developers are building each month with our models across our APIs and key developer products. Our model APIs are now processing approximately 22 billion tokens per minute. That's up from 16 billion just a quarter ago.

key_facts.fact: Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year over year to $24.8 billion, with backlog at $514 billion and nearly 90% of the Fortune 100 using Gemini Enterprise
key_facts.excerpt: Google Cloud saw a meaningful acceleration in growth as revenues increased 82% to $24.8 billion, led by an increase in Google Cloud Platform (GCP) across enterprise AI Solutions and enterprise AI Infrastructure, as well as core GCP services.

key_facts.fact: Alphabet's Q2 free cash flow came in at negative $5.855 billion, versus $10.1 billion positive in the prior quarter
It is the company's first quarter of negative free cash flow since Google went public in 2004; Q2 capex was $44.9 billion, up 100% year over year, and Google bought back no stock in the quarter
key_facts.excerpt: Google stock tumbled Thursday on parent Alphabet's (GOOGL) second-quarter earnings report, which marked the first quarter of negative free cash flow since the company became public in 2004... In Q2, Google reported capital expenditures of $44.9 billion, up 100%, and negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion... Google did not repurchase any of its own stock in Q2 amid the higher capital spending.

key_facts.fact: Alphabet raised 2026 capex guidance to $195-$205 billion from $180-$190 billion; CFO Anat Ashkenazi said 60% of Q2 spending went to servers and 40% to data centers, and that capex will rise significantly again in 2027
key_facts.excerpt: Alphabet's spending on AI is now expected to hit as much as $205bn this year, an increase from $190bn... She said the company spent $45bn in the second quarter, with 60% of the cost going towards servers and the remaining 40% going towards data centres.

key_facts.fact: Pichai said Google has started its most ambitious pre-training run yet, for Gemini 4, and that the company remains supply constrained on compute
key_facts.excerpt: Gemini 3.5 Pro is currently in testing. And our team is already building the next generation of models. We have started our most ambitious pre-training run yet, for Gemini 4... we continue to be supply constrained — a sign of momentum and rapid adoption.

stories.headline: Nearly 200 startups ask Trump not to cut off Chinese open-weight AI models

key_facts.fact: The newly formed Little Tech Association sent letters on Wednesday to President Trump, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and OSTP Director Michael Kratsios urging the administration not to restrict US access to Chinese open-weight AI models
key_facts.excerpt: In a coordinated appeal sent Wednesday, the newly formed Little Tech Association urged President Donald Trump and senior administration officials to reject a blanket ban on Chinese open-weight AI models. The group argues that limiting access would raise costs for startups, reduce competition, and strengthen the market position of a small number of dominant U.S. AI companies.

key_facts.fact: The group counts nearly 200 venture-backed startups, with support from Y Combinator, Proton and Replit; the letters also went to Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent
key_facts.excerpt: Nearly 200 startups including Y Combinator and Proton signed Little Tech Association letters urging Trump not to cut off Chinese open-weight AI models. Letters went to Trump, Commerce Secretary Lutnick, State's Rubio, Treasury's Bessent, and OSTP Director Kratsios, pushing targeted safeguards over broad bans.

key_facts.fact: The letter argues: 'American leadership requires two things: world-leading American open-weight models and continued access for U.S. builders to open models already available worldwide'
key_facts.excerpt: "American leadership requires two things: world-leading American open-weight models and continued access for U.S. builders to open models already available worldwide," the founders wrote in the letter, which was addressed to Trump, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios, and other administration officials.

key_facts.fact: Executive director Harry Godfrey said policymakers should 'use a scalpel, not a hammer', and the group argued banning downloads of Chinese weights would not stop their proliferation
key_facts.excerpt: The association also said banning downloads of Chinese open-weight models would not stop their proliferation, and called for targeted safeguards rather than a blanket prohibition... Harry Godfrey, executive director of the Little Tech Association, said the government "should use a scalpel, not a hammer."

key_facts.fact: Particle founder Suhail Doshi warned hundreds of startups would 'instantly die' if US access to Moonshot's Kimi K3 and similar models were blocked
key_facts.excerpt: Particle founder Suhail Doshi warned hundreds of startups would 'instantly die' if US access to Moonshot's Kimi K3 and similar models is blocked.

key_facts.fact: Senior White House and Cabinet officials discussed the issue earlier in the week; a blanket prohibition on Chinese open-weight models was reportedly not seriously considered
key_facts.excerpt: According to people familiar with internal discussions, senior White House and Cabinet officials discussed the issue earlier this week. A blanket prohibition on Chinese open-weight models was reportedly not seriously considered during those conversations.

key_facts.fact: OSTP Director Michael Kratsios has publicly alleged that Moonshot AI distilled Anthropic's Claude Fable model, an accusation at the center of the debate
key_facts.excerpt: Kratsios has alleged Moonshot distilled Anthropic's Claude model and improperly acquired Nvidia servers, which is the kind of specific IP claim that even a scalpel policy would still have to answer.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches Presence, a hands-on enterprise product for deploying voice and chat agents

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced Presence on Wednesday, a product for deploying and managing AI agents across customer-facing and internal business workflows, available immediately through a limited general availability program
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI has announced Presence, a new enterprise product for deploying and managing AI agents across customer-facing and internal business workflows... Presence is available immediately through a limited general availability program.

key_facts.fact: Deployments are led by OpenAI Forward Deployed Engineers and select global systems integrators; the product is not self-serve
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) and select global systems integrators lead deployments, and the product is not available on a self-service basis.

key_facts.fact: Presence already runs OpenAI's own English-language phone support line and resolves about 75% of inbound support requests without a human, and a Codex-powered improvement loop cut human handoffs by 15 percentage points in 10 days
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI states Presence already resolves 75% of ... issues on its own English-language phone ... line without a human, and that a self-improvement loop powered by its Codex coding tool cut human handoffs by 15 percentage points in 10 days.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is selling Presence through its consulting arm, the OpenAI Deployment Company and its Forward Deployed Engineers, a unit bolstered by the acquisition of consultancy Tomoro in May
key_facts.excerpt: Rather than releasing another self-service API, OpenAI is making Presence available through its consulting arm, the OpenAI Deployment Company and Forward Deployed Engineers, a tech installation workforce that debuted last year and was bolstered by the acquisition of consultancy Tomoro in May.

key_facts.fact: The product supports real-time voice and chat for customer support, outbound sales and high-risk internal workflows, with policies, guardrails, simulations, automated graders and human review before agents go live
key_facts.excerpt: The platform enables companies to create guardrails that block risky AI actions... Presence guardrails also regulate how an agent interacts with the systems that it has permission to access.

key_facts.fact: The launch came one day after OpenAI admitted its own models had autonomously hacked Hugging Face, and OpenAI has not published pricing, interoperability details or service-level commitments
key_facts.excerpt: The launch lands a day after OpenAI admitted its own models had autonomously hacked Hugging Face.

stories.headline: Google pledges $40M and Microsoft $60M in AI credits to the US Genesis Mission for science

key_facts.fact: At the DOE Genesis Mission Summit 2026 on July 22, Google committed $40 million in AI tokens and cloud credits for researchers supporting the Genesis Mission
key_facts.excerpt: Today, at the DOE Genesis Mission Summit 2026, we are expanding this by committing $40 million of AI tokens and cloud credits for researchers in support of the Genesis Mission.

key_facts.fact: Genesis Mission awardees get in-kind access to Google DeepMind's science model portfolio — including AlphaEvolve, AlphaFold 3, AlphaGenome, WeatherNext and AlphaEarth Foundations — and tens of thousands of DOE lab staff get a year of Gemini for Government seats and tokens
key_facts.excerpt: All 17 Department of Energy National Laboratories get access to AlphaEvolve, AlphaFold 3, AlphaGenome, WeatherNext, and AlphaEarth Foundations... Tens of thousands of DOE staff will receive one year of Gemini for Government seats and tokens.

key_facts.fact: The Genesis Mission is the White House national effort to harness AI and double the pace of American scientific discovery within a decade, mobilizing the DOE's 17 national laboratories
key_facts.excerpt: In December, we shared our commitment to the White House's Genesis Mission — the national effort to harness AI and double the pace of American scientific discovery within a decade.

key_facts.fact: At the same July 22 summit, Microsoft pledged $60 million ($40 million in Azure compute and AI credits over three years plus $20 million of engineering and deployment support via a new SPARK program), the Department of Defense committed more than $150 million to Genesis-aligned projects, and NASA formally joined
key_facts.excerpt: At a July 22 summit the White House and DOE announced a shift from planning to early execution with Microsoft pledging $60 million, Google/DeepMind offering $40 million in cloud credits and tokens, NASA formally joining, and the Department of Defense committing more than $150 million to Genesis-aligned projects.

key_facts.fact: Next steps are delivering the pledged credits, running 26 announced challenge tracks, and integrating data, instruments and AI workflows across the 17 national labs
key_facts.excerpt: Officials said the next steps are delivering pledged cloud and compute credits, running the 26 announced challenge tracks, and integrating data, instruments and AI workflows across the 17 national labs.

stories.headline: Google study of 14.6M Gemini chats: AI is used in 68% of occupations but only 21% of tasks

key_facts.fact: Google released ATLAS (Activity, Task, Landscape and Adoption Study), analyzing 14.65 million de-identified interactions across the Gemini app, AI Mode in Search and the Gemini API over two weeks in April
key_facts.excerpt: The report, known as ATLAS — Activity, Task, Landscape and Adoption Study — analyzed 14.65 million de-identified interactions across the Gemini app, Google's AI Mode search experience and the Gemini API over two weeks in April.

key_facts.fact: Work-related activity was mapped to 4,000 tasks across 800 occupations in 150 countries and 140 languages
key_facts.excerpt: Automated systems classified interactions as work-related or non-work-related, then mapped work-related activity to 4,000 tasks across 800 occupations in 150 countries and 140 languages.

key_facts.fact: AI is used in 68% of occupations, which together account for 90% of total US employment, but typically helps with only about 21% of tasks within a job
key_facts.excerpt: Google said AI is now being used across every industry sector and in 68% of occupations that together account for 90% of total US employment. Even so, people are using the technology selectively, with AI typically helping with only about 21% of tasks within a job.

key_facts.fact: Fewer than 10% of workplace interactions involve complete task automation; users mostly rely on AI for brainstorming, strategy, information gathering and learning
key_facts.excerpt: The study found that workplace use is largely focused on collaboration rather than replacing workers. Users most commonly rely on AI for brainstorming, strategy, information gathering and learning, while fewer than 10% of workplace interactions involve complete task automation.

key_facts.fact: Non-work interactions accounted for 86% of Gemini conversations, and Google describes current AI use as 'very shallow'
key_facts.excerpt: Non-work interactions accounted for 86% of Gemini conversations, Google found... he said AI use is also "very shallow," with the average worker using it for only 21% of tasks, with less than 10% of Gemini interactions seemingly geared at automating non-routine cognitive work.

key_facts.fact: Google says AI is serving mainly as a productivity tool that complements workers, while acknowledging future advances could automate a larger share of work and raise questions about entry-level hiring
key_facts.excerpt: The company acknowledged that AI's role in the labor market will likely continue to evolve as the technology improves. Future advances could allow AI systems to automate a larger share of work, while questions remain about the potential impact on entry-level hiring and career development.
